title: When the way is lost
hookLine: when the great Tao is forgotten, rules about kindness and duty appear (Tao Te Ching 18)

lines: WHOEVER IS EATING MY YOGURT, STOP.
cards: A sign taped to an office fridge: please label your food. Below it, a second sign: please don't take food that isn't yours. Below that, in red: whoever is eating my yogurt, stop.
Nobody wrote those signs on day one. On day one, people just didn't take each other's lunches. Each sign marks the spot where something was already lost.
Chapter eighteen of the Tao Te Ching is only a few lines long, and it reads every sign like that one.

teach.h: THE WAY IS LOST, AND KINDNESS GETS NAMED.
teach.b: First, the opening line. When the great Way is abandoned, the chapter says, kindness and righteousness appear. That sounds backward.
Aren't those good things? They are. The point is about when people start talking about them.
On this reading, no one needs speeches about kindness where kindness is simply how things are; the speeches start once it's gone missing. Second, the pattern repeats.
When cleverness and know-how show up, great pretending follows. When families fall out of harmony, people start praising devoted children and loving parents.
When a country falls into disorder, loyal ministers get noticed.

teach.h: EACH VIRTUE SHOWS UP WHEN IT'S MISSED.
teach.b: Each virtue becomes visible, and gets a name and a rule, at the moment its absence is felt. Third, who's listening.

teach.h: REN AND YI: A CONVERSATION OF SCHOOLS.
teach.b: Kindness and righteousness, ren and yi, are words the school of Confucius treasured, and some readers hear this chapter as part of a conversation between the two schools.
Confucian teachers have their own answer: that naming and practicing virtue is how people grow into it. The Tao Te Ching's line is that the naming comes late. Fourth, the hint inside.
If rules about kindness are a sign the way was lost, the way itself is something before the rule.

Not unkindness, and not a world without rules: a kindness that came first, before anyone needed to write it on the fridge. The chapter leaves a question: can a person find their way back to that, one small act at a time?

how: Some readers of the Tao Te Ching use chapter eighteen as a check on themselves: they notice when they do good only because a rule says so, and look for kindness that comes before any rule.

games.q: what does “when the way is lost” mean?
o: a warning against breaking the laws of the land
rules about kindness show up after the way is gone
a traveler's prayer for finding the road home

s: chapter eighteen says kindness is bad
it says talk of kindness appears once the way is lost. the way is something before the rule.
the chapter's virtues each become visible when they're missed
devoted children are praised when families fall out of harmony.
ren and yi are words the school of Confucius treasured
some readers hear the chapter as part of a conversation between the two schools.

games.q: the office fridge has three signs about not taking food. by chapter eighteen's light, what do the signs tell you?
o: the office is very well run.
something was lost before the signs went up.
games.why: when the great Way is abandoned, kindness and righteousness appear. each rule marks a spot where something went missing.

practice: Think of one small kindness you could do that no rule asks of you, not because it's polite or someone's watching, just because it fits: refilling the coffee pot, holding a door a little longer, a message to someone who's been quiet.
Hold that one act in mind, and notice whether it feels different from the ones you do because you're supposed to.

wordCard.voice: When the way is lost. Chapter eighteen's warning: the rules about kindness and duty show up after the thing they describe has gone missing. Today's word.

orig.note: Chinese: the great Way, the Tao, which chapter eighteen says has been abandoned when kindness and duty get named.
